title: Weekly Deep Dive: Is Jet Fuel About to Break the Airline Industry?
summary: Jet fuel prices are spiking hard enough to trigger layoffs at Alaska and AirBaltic, pay freezes at Ryanair, and route cuts at WestJet and Flydubai — all in the same week. Ryan and Hope dig into whether this is a temporary squeeze or a structural shift that reshapes fleets, bankrupts weaker carriers, and ends the A321XLR era before it even gets started.

topic.topic: Jet fuel prices are spiking dramatically, forcing airlines to cut routes, freeze pay, and lay off workers—this is becoming an existential threat to airline profitability.
topic.why: Fuel costs have been mentioned in at least 8+ articles this week as a direct driver of route cuts (WestJet, Flydubai), layoffs (Alaska 200 jobs, AirBaltic 300), pay freezes (Ryanair), and fare hikes. The Air Current explicitly warned aviation is 'on the verge of a correction.' Unlike temporary headwinds, this touches every airline's P&L simultaneously and forces strategic choices that reshape networks.
key_facts: Ryanair cited a $2 billion fuel cost hit from Middle East conflict, triggering pay freezes and cost cuts
WestJet cancelled 15 international routes; Alaska laid off 200 employees; Frontier posted $104M loss despite record revenue
Multiple airlines (Frontier, JetBlue) posting losses despite high ticket prices, signaling fuel inflation is outpacing revenue
Heathrow, SkyTeam, and other infrastructure players are making simultaneous structural decisions under fuel pressure
The spike is forcing legacy carriers to rethink fleet strategy (delta skipping A321XLR, Southwest considering widebody despite decades of 737-only policy)
